Indigenous Tolaki lands face environmental harm while carmakers pledge audits and supply chain reviews.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: An investigation revealed that nickel from the Cahaya and Hengjaya mines in Sulawesi, Indonesia, enters supply chains for carmakers including Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla. The ore is processed locally and in China by Huayou before reaching battery manufacturers such as CATL. Satellite data shows mining has caused extensive deforestation on indigenous Tolaki lands.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Carmakers use nickel in cathodes to boost battery range, but increased mining threatens primary rainforests and biodiversity. Forest loss from mining operations may multiply nickel's carbon footprint up to 500 times compared with earlier estimates, while also harming local indigenous livelihoods.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.text: The scandal damages the Premier League's reputation and fan trust. Because the club is owned by the Abu Dhabi United Group, it also raises international relations issues and questions regarding foreign state influence over major British institutions.

articles.title: Teen's death inspires mum's drive for earlier rare cancer diagnosis
articles.standfirst: Hannah York hopes new guidance will help doctors spot signs of soft tissue sarcomas sooner.

gist: Hannah York campaigns for early rare cancer diagnosis following her daughter Liberty's death.
Liberty York passed away from a rare soft tissue sarcoma shortly after her nineteenth birthday.
New guidelines aim to help healthcare professionals recognise childhood sarcomas much earlier.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Nineteen-year-old Liberty York developed a rare and aggressive soft tissue sarcoma after initially experiencing fatigue and nausea. Medical staff initially suspected other conditions including mastitis and hormone issues, which delayed her diagnosis until a large tumour formed. Despite surgery, the cancer spread to her lungs and she died in June 2025.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rare cancers in young people can be misdiagnosed because symptoms resemble more common health issues. Early detection is critical for aggressive sarcomas to give patients a better fighting chance.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Liberty's mother is channelling her grief into campaigning for earlier diagnoses and supports new guidelines from the Children and Young People's Cancer Association to improve recognition among healthcare professionals.
